Greece.title: Greece
Greece.text: In mythological times, Greece existed in a world where gods and humans interacted directly, and natural phenomena were interpreted as divine signs. The pantheon of Greek gods, goddesses, heroes, and monsters played a central role in shaping the lives and behaviors of Greek people. These myths were integral to the Greek's understanding of the world around them, providing explanations for natural events, cultural traditions, and societal norms. [[Mount Olympus]] was considered the home of the gods, and many myths revolved around their interactions with humans. These stories were often depicted in Greek art and literature, serving as moral or cautionary tales.
Greece.summary: In mythological times, Greek mythology shaped societal understanding through divine interactions, pantheon influence, and cultural narratives centered around Mount Olympus, with myths serving as moral and explanatory tales in art and literature.

Heaven.title: Heaven
Heaven.text: The realm of Afterlife where souls who are good throughout their physical lives. Home to all angellic beings such as [[Archangels]] who serve [[God]]. The main hub where [[God]] watches over his creations.
Heaven.summary: The Afterlife realm is a divine abode for virtuous souls, housing angellic beings like Archangels who serve God and act as His primary hub for overseeing creation.

Hell's Palace.title: Hell's Palace
Hell's Palace.text: Home to [[Lucifer]] which resides in [[Hell]]. It has many facilities suited for the 'King of Hell' allowing him to watch over [[Hell]]. It was intended to be [[Lucifer]]'s prison.
Hell's Palace.summary: Hell serves as Lucifer's residence, equipped with facilities to oversee his domain and originally intended as his prison.

Hell.title: Hell
Hell.text:
The deep dark pits of hell where only the cruel and creped live with the only intent to cause pain, suffering and chaos to those who are deemed weaker and fragile. Yes. This is Hell. The ruler of Hell is an evil tyrant who is deemed the "King of Hell" and the most powerful demon to exist on such a scorching plain of existence... or is he?...

It can be seen as either the scorching fires of hell or the ice cold of the damned and unsalvageable souls who are destined for eternal suffering. The realm appears as whatever the person sees as a "nightmare" and worst possible scenario. This will make that nightmare play over and over again for eternity, causing pain and suffering for the rest of their souls' existence.
Hell.summary: Hell is a tormenting realm where cruel beings eternally torment the weak through personalized nightmares, ruled by an ambiguous tyrant whose domain manifests as either scorching fire or icy despair.

Mount Olympus.title: Mount Olympus
Mount Olympus.text:
Where the [[Titanomarchy War]] happens and where [[Pixie Dixie (Johnny)]] dies.

Mount Olympus being the home to the [[Olympians]] and their spoils of higher existence watching over the humans in [[Greece]]. Living in luxury and peace.
Mount Olympus.summary: The Titanomarchy War occurs and Pixie Dixie (Johnny) dies in the realm of Mount Olympus, where the Olympians reside in luxury, overseeing humanity in Greece.

The Final Resting Place.title: The Final Resting Place
The Final Resting Place.text: This is a location in ties with my own personal perception of peace, where the water droplets are so tranquil and faint that the sound reaches your soul's ears and not just your physical realm. where the dock stands sturdy but creeks to let the walkers know of its presence. the lake still yet alive full of fish and plants, breathing through the lungs of the earth, oozing with life. the moon never leaves and has locked the sun out of the home with not even a peep through the windows. The moon sparkles and shines like a light bulb with an idea to impress the habiters of earth. there is no one but I to be impressed by. The sky is full of stars and galaxies that no man could ever dream of touching yet was all in an eyes distance of sight. it was like my eyes were slowing becoming telescopes being drawn into them and extended out of curiosity. the trees surrounding the lake and cabin are chatty yet respectful of my space, their words come out as leaves leave their branches and their sentences form natures greatest calling, to carry on the seed and grow into their own tree. the cabin is a quaint country rustic-looking cottage where no one but air and void have lived in it. inside though is a cosy atmosphere with logs ready to burn and crackle by the fireplace like a beautiful performance put on stage by the best fire dancers in the world. the walls were aged but just like the trees around us i could tell they were related to each other, with fine aging comes finer quality. there was two bedrooms, one was decorated as the main space for sleeping and resting whilst also keeping warm and comfy on those lazy days. the second room was more of a spare that didn't have the intention of anyone coming to test it but it was made just in case... I get the feeling no one did come though as the layer of dust on top of the bed, dresser and wardrobe was like a field of snow that with one blow could all fly away to the greatest heights of the skies and stars.
The Final Resting Place.summary: This secluded, tranquil lakeside cabin, surrounded by whispering trees and a moonlit sky, embodies a personal sanctuary of peace where nature's quiet beauty and untouched stillness create an intimate, almost otherworldly atmosphere.

Transylvania.title: Transylvania
Transylvania.text:
15th century Transylvania where the strigoi are plentiful in numbers and The Lord of Darkness is at his strongest. The place where horrors are born and raised. The dark anywhere else in the world would seem like heaven and daylight compared to even the brightest of days in Transylvania. Home to some of the most notorious mythological and folklore creatures throughout history. This is where horror was born. 

[[Werewolves]], [[Ghouls]],[[Vampire]] and other monsters roam this era and place.

This is where the party meet the new female additions to the party; [[Elvenor]] the battle master elf and [[Klaudia Blutdieb]] the noble [[Vampire]].
Transylvania.summary: In 15th century Transylvania, a realm of horrors ruled by the Lord of Darkness and teeming with strigoi, werewolves, ghouls, and vampires, the party encounters Elvenor, the battle master elf, and Klaudia Blutdieb, the noble vampire.

Baba Yaga.title: Baba Yaga
Baba Yaga.text:
Baba Yaga is a witch, known in Eastern Slavic countries. In majority of tales, she is represented as an evil being who ride either broom or mortar, wields a pestle and scares and eat children, however in very few tales she gives her wisdom to protagonists. She lives in forest hut which has chicken legs.

Children are warned in Russia that Babayka (or Baba Yaga) will come for them at night if they behave badly.

Poland – _"Baba Jaga"_ or _"Muma"_ is a monster (often portrayed as a witch living in the forest) that kidnaps badly behaving children and presumably eats them. It is referenced in a children's game of the same name, which involves one child being blindfolded, and other children trying to avoid being caught.
Baba Yaga.summary: Baba Yaga is a feared witch in Eastern Slavic folklore, typically depicted as an evil creature who rides a broom or mortar, uses a pestle, and kidnaps or eats children, though occasionally grants wisdom to protagonists, with cultural variations in Russia and Poland.

Chimera.summary: The creature is a lion with a ram's head (sharp teeth, rock-breaking headbutt), a snake's head (venom/acid spitting), and a dragon's head (fire-breathing, scent-detection).

Kikimora.title: Kikimora
Kikimora.text:
Kikimora is a mythical creature from Slavic folklore, typically depicted as a female spirit with a somewhat sinister reputation. The origin of the name "Kikimora" is unclear, but it has ties to Russian and Eastern European traditions. She is often associated with domestic settings, particularly with the home and household activities.

Kikimora's appearance varies in different tales, but she's usually portrayed as a small, ghostly woman with disheveled hair and tattered clothing, sometimes appearing as a bird-like figure with a long beak or feathers. Her demeanor ranges from mischievous to malevolent, depending on the context.

In folklore, Kikimora is known to inhabit homes, often appearing at night or in dreams. She is typically linked to disorder and chaos, causing disturbances in the household, such as unexplained noises, broken objects, or sudden messes. Some stories depict her as weaving or spinning, which can either bring fortune or misfortune, depending on her mood.

Kikimora is sometimes considered a harbinger of bad luck or misfortune. Her presence in a home can be seen as a warning of impending trouble or unrest. To ward her off or calm her down, homeowners might employ various rituals, such as tidying the house, leaving offerings, or reciting prayers.

Overall, Kikimora is a complex figure in Slavic folklore, embodying both the domestic and the uncanny, with her presence serving as a reminder of the unseen forces that might dwell within the home.
Kikimora.summary: Kikimora is a Slavic mythical creature associated with domestic chaos and misfortune, depicted as a mischievous or malevolent spirit inhabiting homes and causing disturbances, often requiring rituals to appease or ward off.

Kitsune.title: Kitsune

Therion.text: Therion is the Pre-Existential Beast considered to be the first monster within all of Creation as well as the monstrous and most primal side of [[God]]. He is also the primal beast that spawned equally destructive creatures of darkness known to John of Patmos as Trihexa and Divus.
Therion.summary: Therion is the Pre-Existential Beast, the primal and destructive origin of all monsters in Creation, embodying the monstrous side of God and spawning entities like Trihexa and Divus.

Treant.title: Treant
Treant.text: Treants are **imaginary beings from fantasy literature**. In name it arises from the union of the English words "tree" (tree) and "giant" (giant). They are described as large trees capable of moving, in some cases with the roots, and in other cases with the legs and feet.
Treant.summary: Treants are imaginary fantasy beings derived from "tree" and "giant," depicted as large movable trees with roots or legs.

Vampire.title: Vampire
Vampire.text:
Also known as 'strigoi' in Romanian the blood sucking monsters are dead and vulnerable sunlight. They are more night creatures and therefore don’t often be seen during the daylight.

They are often associated with the mammals bats. A famous vampire is [[Count Dracula]] who may be Vlad the Impaler due to the similarity of impaling people with stakes. [[Count Dracula]] is a fictional character made from a book written by Bram Stoker.

These creatures drink blood in order to gain strength and stay young allowing them to live up to 1000-5000 years old and [[Count Dracula]] being one of the strongest vampires to walk the earth is estimated to be 591 years old. Here are some of their abilities -

- See in the dark 
- Quick reflexes
- Near point immortality
- Able to drink blood to gain more years of life and heal wounds
- Incredibly strong
- Has fangs and claws that extend from their nails
Vampire.summary: Vampires, also known as strigoi, are nocturnal, blood-drinking creatures vulnerable to sunlight, associated with bats, and depicted in folklore and fiction like Count Dracula, who gains strength and longevity through blood consumption and possesses abilities such as night vision, near immortality, and enhanced physical traits.

Werecat.title: Werecat
Werecat.text: A werecat is defined as **a person that turns into a cat**. They fall into the overarching category of therianthropy, the mythical ability to transform into an animal by shapeshifting.
Werecat.summary: A werecat is a person who transforms into a cat, classified under therianthropy as a mythical ability to shapeshift into animals.

Werewolves.title: Werewolves
Werewolves.text: A werewolf, also known as a lycanthrope ("wolf-man"), is a mythological or folkloric human with the ability to shape shift into a wolf or an therianthropic hybrid wolf-like creature, either purposely or after being placed under a curse or affliction (e.g. via a bite or scratch from another werewolf). This transformation is often associated with the appearance of the full moon.
Werewolves.summary: A werewolf, or lycanthrope, is a mythical human capable of transforming into a wolf or hybrid creature through curse, bite, or scratch, often linked to the full moon.

Surget Michael proavi mei hereditabit et percussisti omnes adversantes mihi veram et gladio et ego deferam exercitum mandatum Amen

Words For Mikey.title: Words For Mikey
Words For Mikey.text:
Kitsune! Ā, ikani anata wa anata no inari o hanareru no ka! Anata no hontō no sugata o misete, -shin no sugata ni modotte, kore ni chikadzukanaide kudasai!

meaning

How dare you leave your inari! Show your true form and go back to your kami form and stay out of this!
Words For Mikey.summary: The Kitsune is confronted for abandoning their inari form, ordered to reveal their true form, return to their kami form, and stay out of the situation.

Gaea.title: Gaea
Gaea.text: Gaia, also known as Gaea, was a primordial deity in ancient Greek mythology, representing the Earth. She was the mother of [[Uranus]], the sky, and with him, she gave birth to the other gods and goddesses, including the Titans, Cyclopes, and Giants. She played a crucial role in the overthrowing of [[Uranus]] and later, Titan [[Cronus]]. She was revered as a nurturing mother figure and was often depicted as a robust woman emerging from the earth.
Gaea.summary: Gaia, the primordial Earth deity in Greek mythology, was the mother of Uranus and other cosmic beings, played a key role in overthrowing Uranus and Cronus, and was revered as a nurturing mother figure emerging from the earth.

Uranus.title: Uranus
Uranus.text: Uranus was a primordial deity in ancient Greek mythology, representing the sky. He was the son and mate of Gaia, the earth. Together, they created many of the other gods and goddesses, including the Titans, the Cyclopes, and the Giants. Uranus was overthrown by his son Cronus, who castrated him and threw his genitals into the sea, an act that gave birth to Aphrodite. Uranus was the first ruler of the universe, and his name became synonymous with the heavens.
Uranus.summary: Uranus, a primordial Greek sky deity and son of Gaia, co-created the Titans and other gods, was overthrown by his son Cronus, whose castration led to Aphrodite's birth, and became synonymous with the heavens.

Chiron.title: Chiron
Chiron.text:
Chiron is the son of the Titan Cronus and the Sea Nymph Philyra and is a centaur with his front two legs still human as well as his upper body and his lower body and two back legs are of a horse. He is famed for his wisdom and knowledge in medicine. He is civilised compared to other centaurs and is extremely skilled in marksmanship and hunting.

Abilities:

•Speed matching of a horse

•Incredible marksman skills especially with a bow

•Wise

•Knowledgeable of medicine

•Blood of a Titan and Sea Nymph so he is incredibly strong and able to breath in water
Chiron.summary: Chiron, the half-human, half-horse centaur son of Cronus and Philyra, is renowned for his wisdom, medical expertise, exceptional marksmanship, and extraordinary abilities including speed, strength, and underwater breathing.

Count Dracula.title: Count Dracula
Count Dracula.text:
A fictional character in Bram Stoker's 'Dracula' book who is known as the strongest vampire in history and was known as 'Vlad the Impaler' for he was known to impale his enemies with stakes on the battlefield. 

he is estimated to be around 591 years old and could well easily live up to 5000. He lives in [[Transylvania]] where his castle is located and preys on the local villages however, some of the villages give sacrifices to Dracula for the hopes of peace and security in return he receives fresh young humans from their settlements as food to prevent him from hunting on hunger.

In this novel he is one of [[Lucifer]]'s commanders and therefore [[Jonathon McBride]] needs to kill Dracula in order to gain his key. Dracula will be [[Jonathon McBride]]'s hardest fight yet and it will require all of his companions to help with it too.
Count Dracula.summary: Dracula, a fictional vampire from Bram Stoker's novel, is the strongest vampire in history, known as Vlad the Impaler, residing in Transylvania where he preys on villages for sustenance and is a commander of Lucifer, requiring Jonathan McBride's allies to defeat him for a critical key.

Lucifer.title: Lucifer
Lucifer.text: He is the ruler of Hell, titled as the most powerful demon to exist and also one of the ex-archangels who had fallen and made to watch over hell as punishment for going against god. Lucifer is also known as the sin of Pride and made in the image and power of God which gave him the ego and pride that makes him think he is the best of the best, which is why he tried to overpower God and rule Heaven. That Failed. As punishment for treason against God, he was sent down from heaven and exiled to rule Hell for all Eternity.
Lucifer.summary: Lucifer, once an ex-archangel exiled for rebelling against God due to his pride and desire to rule Heaven, now rules Hell as the most powerful demon eternally punished for his treason.

Pied Piper.title: Pied Piper
Pied Piper.text:
Pied Piper known to have lured a town’s children into danger and under control just with his magical flute, he is known as a bitter and tricky man. He teams up with the [[Puppet Master]] and turns the towns children into puppets and [[Ghouls]] which do their bidding, terrorising the locals who live within the forest.

Abilities:

•Can play a magical flute which can has many abilities including taking control, wiping their memory and even putting people to sleep.

•His Jester like clothes lets him blend into his surroundings and turns him invisible.

•Can turn kids into [[Ghouls]] every blue moon (during the red moon they turn into vampire underlings who then serve [[Count Dracula]]).
Pied Piper.summary: Pied Piper, a bitter and tricky man with a magical flute capable of controlling, memory-wiping, and sleep-inducing, teams up with the Puppet Master to turn children into puppets, ghouls, and lunar-vampire underlings, terrorizing the forest town's inhabitants.

Puppet Master.title: Puppet Master
Puppet Master.text:
Known to make and control puppets through the uses of pivots and string, the puppeteer is able to entertain any age group however, he isn’t just an entertainer…

With the abilities to turn living things into puppets and control them like dolls the puppeteer has [[Pinnochio]] under his control and he’s the perfect toy to go unnoticed but Jonathon and his friends see through the trickster

Abilities:

•Can turn any piece of wood into a golem of that appropriate size.

•Can turn living things into puppets.

•Able to control any of his puppets and decide when they die.

•Really skilled in using string made from spider silk which can be stronger than steel.
Puppet Master.summary: The puppeteer, skilled in crafting and controlling puppets via pivots, spider silk strings, and transforming wood/living beings into golems, secretly manipulates Pinocchio as a hidden puppet while outwitting Jonathon and his friends.

Razel.title: Razel
Razel.text:
He is the brother and new ruler of the Atlantic city. Capable of controlling people and brainwashing them. Illusionist and trickster of the fisher people. Known to eat his own kind to survive.

•Can hypnotise

•Able to manipulate your dreams

•Cannibal

•Water manipulation
Razel.summary: NEMO is the cannibalistic, hypnotic ruler of Atlantic City, a trickster and illusionist with powers over dreams, water manipulation, and brainwashing.

Skadi.title: Skadi
Skadi.text: Known as the Goddess of the winter, skiing, and hunting. She is the daughter of the [[Jotun]] known as [[Thjazi]]. After he was killed by the [[Aesir Gods]] she was promised that 1. his eyes would be casted into the sky and turned into stars and 2. she would be able to marry one of the gods however only by their feet could she choose.  She married a man and was later divorced. In this story she is the kidnapper of [[Jonathon McBride]] and with the help of her dad they tried to kill and eat humans over the years and [[Jonathon McBride]] was next unless he became her friend which later would’ve been her husband. After [[Jonathon McBride]] killing the father-eagle like beast he was powerful enough to face the daughter in which in the end he managed to kill her after facing her in battle.
Skadi.summary: The Goddess of winter, skiing, and hunting, daughter of Thjazi, sought vengeance against the Aesir for her father's death, attempted to kill humans with her father, and was ultimately slain by Jonathon McBride after he defeated the father-eagle beast and confronted her in battle.

Thjazi.title: Thjazi
Thjazi.text:
A powerful [[Jotun]] that is able to morph into an eagle. The tale is that he tricked the three Gods of Loki, Odin and Hoenir into luring the Goddess of youth and rejuvenation out into a forest where Thjazi kidnaps her leaving all the Aesir Gods without apples, the Gods are not able to feel the immortal vigour they’re used to so they hunt down who’s responsible, who is Loki, and they force him to save the Goddess Idunn and with the help of a falcon suit Loki is able to fly to the mountains and save her. However, Thjazi begins to chase Loki and Idunn and thus enters the city of the gods, [[Asgard]], and falls into a trap set by the other Gods which is successful and burns the eagle, leaving it vulnerable for the Gods to finish the beast off and they cast the eyes into the sky to form new stars as a form of apology for his daughter [[Skadi]].

He is one of [[Lucifer]]'s commanders and kidnaps [[Jonathon McBride]] taking him to the [[Norway]] and keeping him in a cabin to eat just like the other unfortunate victims of Thjazi but is killed by [[Jonathon McBride]] and [[Mickey]] and they escape to later kill [[Skadi]] too.
Thjazi.summary: Thjazi, a Jotun with eagle abilities, tricks the Aesir gods into kidnapping Idunn, is defeated and his eyes become stars, later serving as Lucifer's commander before being killed by Jonathon McBride and Mickey, who also kill his daughter Skadi.
